He played eleven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and he won an [[NBA Finals|NBA championship]] when he played for the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2022. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]] and was selected with the third overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]]. ==High school career== Porter attended [[Scott County Central High School]], whose district includes the small communities of [[Morley, Missouri|Morley]], [[Vanduser, Missouri|Vanduser]], [[Haywood City, Missouri|Haywood City]], and parts of rural [[Sikeston, Missouri|Sikeston]]. He earned all-state honors as a junior and senior, leading the Braves to three straight Class 1 state championships and giving Scott Central its state-record 15th title overall. During his senior year, he helped lead the Braves to 29–2 record, averaging 30 points and 14 rebounds a game.{{cite web|url=http://www.standard-democrat.com/story/1800070.html|title=Top sports stories of 2011: No. 2 – Otto Porter|date=December 31, 2011 |access-date=February 24, 2013}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Porter was listed as the No. 8 power forward and the No. 37 player in the nation in 2011.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Otto-Porter-108410 Otto Porter Recruiting Profile] ==College career== He signed a letter of intent with the [[Georgetown Hoyas]] and played his first game with them on November 12, 2011, against [[Savannah State Tigers basketball|Savannah State]], recording 9 points, 8 rebounds and 3 blocks. Rounding out his freshman year, Porter averaged 9.7 [[points per game]] and 6.8 [[rebounds per game]]. As a sophomore, he nearly doubled his points production, averaging 16.2 points and 7.5 rebounds per game. At the conclusion of the 2012–13 season, Porter led his team to a 25–7 record and a number 2 seed in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. For his efforts, he was named the [[Big East Player of the Year]] and was a finalist for both the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] and [[Wooden Award]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.org/tabid/435/article/242780/Georgetown-s-Otto-Porter-Named-Player-of-the-Year.aspx|title=Georgetown's Otto Porter Named Player of the Year|access-date=June 28, 2013|archive-date=June 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130628040236/http://www.bigeast.org/tabid/435/article/242780/Georgetown-s-Otto-Porter-Named-Player-of-the-Year.aspx|url-status=dead}} Porter recorded 13 points and 11 rebounds in a first round upset loss to the 15th-seeded [[2012–13 Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball team|Florida Gulf Coast]].{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2013|agency=Associated Press |title=Florida Gulf Coast stuns Georgetown; 7th No. 15 seed to beat No. 2 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330810046 |access-date=June 28, 2013 |website=ESPN.com}} On April 15, 2013, Porter announced his decision to forgo his final two years of eligibility and enter the [[NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2013–2019)=== [[File:Otto Porter Jr. (15537042458).jpg|thumb|right|Porter with the Wizards in 2014]] Porter was selected with the third overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-2013-draft-picks-otto-porter-glen-rice-jr|title=Wizards Sign 2013 Draft Picks Otto Porter & Glen Rice Jr.|website=www.nba.com}} However, he missed training camp and the first 18 games of the 2013–14 season with a hip injury. He made his NBA debut on December 6, going scoreless in 14 minutes in a 109–105 overtime loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20131206/MILWAS/gameinfo.html Notebook: Bucks 109, Wizards 105] He twice scored a season-high nine points in April 2014.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/porteot01/gamelog/2014/|title=Otto Porter Jr. 2013-14 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On November 1, 2014, he scored 19 of his career-high 21 points in the second half of the Wizards' 108–97 win over the Bucks.[http://www.nba.com/games/20141101/MILWAS/gameinfo.html Paul Pierce ejected; Wizards top Bucks 108-97] On November 7, 2015, he set a new career high with 23 points in a 114–99 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20151107/WASATL/gameinfo.html Hawks beat Wizards 114-99 for 7th straight win] On December 12, 2015, he scored a career-high 28 points in a 114–111 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20151212/WASDAL/gameinfo.html Porter, Wall lead Wizards past Mavericks, 114-111][[File:Isaiah Thomas, Otto Porter Jr. (34419856896).jpg|thumbnail|right|Porter in May 2017]] On November 9, 2016, Porter scored a career-high 34 points in a 118–93 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899557|title=Celtics 93-118 Wizards (Nov 9, 2016) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} On December 26, he had 32 points, made a career-high five three-pointers and grabbed 13 rebounds in a 107–102 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899903|title=Bucks 102-107 Wizards (Dec 26, 2016) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} On January 18, he set a new career high with six three-pointers to finish with 25 points in a 104–101 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400900049|title=Grizzlies 101-104 Wizards (Jan 18, 2017) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} He made six three-pointers for the second straight night on January 19, finishing with 23 points in a 113–110 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400900059|title=Wizards 113-110 Knicks (Jan 19, 2017) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} He started 80 games and set career highs in scoring (13.4 points per game), rebounds (6.4) and steals (1.5) while shooting 51.6 percent from the field and 43.4 percent from three-point range in 2016–17. According to ESPN's Real Plus-Minus, a player's estimated on-court impact on team performance, Porter was the most efficient scorer in the NBA among 115 players with at least 800 possessions, penetrating defenses in transition and as a spot-up shooter.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/fancy-stats/wp/2017/07/05/even-with-his-max-deal-otto-porter-jr-will-be-underpaid/|title=Analysis {{!}} Even with his max deal, Otto Porter Jr. will be underpaid|last=Greenberg|first=Neil|date=July 5, 2017|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=September 15, 2017|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}} His three-point shooting percentage was fourth best in the NBA.{{Cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/leaders/#!?Season=2016-17&SeasonType=Regular%20Season&StatCategory=FG3_PCT&PerMode=Totals|title=NBA.com/Stats {{!}} Season Leaders|website=stats.nba.com|language=en|access-date=September 15, 2017}} On July 4, 2017, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] offered Porter a four-year, $106.5 million contract, the maximum they could give him.{{cite web|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2017/07/04/otto-porters-free-agency-prospects-have-dimmed-will-the-nets-offer-the-max/|title=Otto Porter Jr. agrees to max contract with Brooklyn Nets. exchange for [[Nikola Vučević]] and [[Al-Farouq Aminu]]. Orlando also received two future first-round draft picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-acquire-wendell-carter-jr-otto-porter-jr-chicago-bulls-nikola-vucevic-al-farouq-aminu-trade-20210325|title=Magic Acquire Wendell Carter Jr., Otto Porter Jr. and Two First Round Draft Picks From Chicago|date=March 25, 2021|work=NBA.com}} ===Golden State Warriors (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Porter signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] on a $2.4 million veteran minimum contract.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward Otto Porter Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/otto-porter-jr-20210806|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2021|date=August 6, 2021}}{{Cite web |last=Poole |first=Monte |date=August 10, 2021 |title=Porter Jr. 'absolutely' has something to prove with Warriors |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/warriors-otto-porter-jr-absolutely-has-something-prove |access-date=February 27, 2022 |website=NBC Sports}} Porter won an [[NBA championship]] when the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in 6 games of the [[2022 NBA Finals]]. He played a sizable role in the postseason, starting in Game 6 of the Finals.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}} ===Toronto Raptors (2022–2024)=== On July 6, 2022, Porter signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on a two-year, $12.4 million contract.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN PORTER JR.|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-porter-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}} On January 10, 2023, after playing only eight games in the season, he underwent season-ending surgery on his left foot.{{cite web|title=Raptors' Otto Porter Jr. undergoes season-ending surgery on left foot|url=https://www.nba.com/news/raptors-otto-porter-jr-left-foot-injury|website=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2023}} On February 8, 2024, Porter was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] alongside [[Kira Lewis Jr.]] and a 2024 first-round draft pick in exchange for [[Kelly Olynyk]] and [[Ochai Agbaji]].{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kira Lewis Jr., Otto Porter 2024}} However, he did not play any games for the Jazz{{cite web|title=Otto Porter Jr.|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/porteot01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 11, 2024}} and was waived on March 11, 2024.{{cite 32.5 || .498 || .355 || .751 || 7.1 || 2.1 || 1.5 || .9 || 12.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Porter comes from a family with many accomplishments in basketball. His father, Otto Porter Sr., was part of [[Scott County Central High School]]'s first title in 1976 and holds the high school record with 1,733 rebounds. His mother, Elnora Porter (née Timmons), helped the same school win the 1984 state championship.{{cite news |last=Buckner|first=Candace|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2018/10/17/otto-porter-jr-plays-right-way-more-is-expected-max-player/|title=Otto Porter Jr. plays 'the right way.' But more is expected of a max player.|work=washingtonpost.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=November 25, 2018}} His uncles [[Marcus Timmons]] and Donnie McClinton won a combined six state championships.{{cite news|url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/scott-county-central-s-porter-a-top-prospect/article_b8448e88-fd62-5f33-89b7-066cf98563d1.html|title=Scott County Central's Porter a top prospect |access-date=November 23, 2018 | work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|first1=Stu|last1=Durando|date=April 11, 2011}} Additionally, his uncles Melvin Porter and Jerry Porter, and his younger brother Jeffery Porter, have also won state titles. First cousin Calvin Porter Jr. was one of three Porters to start for the high school's championship team in 2011. His cousin Mark Mosely was the starting point guard for the Braves in 1990 and 1991 when they won state championships. His cousins Corey and Reece Porter{{cite web|url=http://www.standard-democrat.com/story/1710318.html|title=Corey Porter continues family legacy|date=March 14, 2011 |access-date=September 10, 2013}}{{cite news | title = Jeffery Porter is making a name for himself during Scott County Central's final four run | work =Southeast Missourian | location = Cape Girardeau, Missouri | date = March 11, 2015}} helped [[Sikeston High School]] win its first state title in its first undefeated season. His cousin Michael Porter, the son of [[Drury University]] basketball player Melvin Porter, was a former four-time all-state basketball player for Sikeston High School who later played for [[Southeast Missouri State University]].{{cite web|url=https://www.southeastarrow.com/story/1942624.html|title=Southeast basketball player is out for the season|date=February 19, 2013 |access-date=November 17, 2021}}{{cite web|url=http://www.standard-democrat.com/blogs/pobst/entry/53709/|title=Many knew this day would come for Otto Porter, Jr.|date=June 28, 2013 |access-date=September 10, 2013}} His cousins Dominique Porter and Jaylen Porter played basketball for the [[Culver–Stockton College|Culver-Stockton]] Wildcats.{{cite web|url=http://www.cscwildcats.com/roster/17/23/2965.php|title=Culver-Stockton Wildcat Athletics: Dominique Porter|access-date=November 23, 2018}}{{cite web | last=Duerr | first=Chris | title=The Climb is All There Is... (Duerrisms for September 5th) | website=KHQA | date=2013-09-05 | url=https://khqa.com/sports/overtime-blog/the-climb-is-all-there-is-duerrisms-for-september-5th | access-date=2024-11-01}} His cousin and former teammate Bobby Hatchett played for [[Midland College]], which played for the National Junior College Athletic Association national championship.
